answers.question: What is the mechanism for?
answers.answer: It keeps the service's log from filling the disk by closing the file from time to time, putting it aside under a dated name and starting a new one.
quotes: The service writes its log into one file, and a file that only grows fills the disk.
So the service closes the file from time to time, puts it aside under a dated name and starts a new one.

answers.question: What does it take in, and what does it keep?
answers.answer: It takes in one event, a line to be written, and keeps the size of the current file and the time that file was opened.
quotes: The mechanism keeps the size of the current file and the time it was opened.
It takes in one event, a line to be written.

answers.question: By which steps does it reach its result?
answers.answer: Before each line it checks the current file against 100 megabytes and one day; under both it writes the line to the current file; over either it closes the file, renames it with the date and time of closing, opens a new file and writes the line there.
quotes: The mechanism is five steps and two limits.
Before each line the service checks the current file against two limits, 100 megabytes and one day.
Under both limits it writes the line into the current file.
Over either limit it closes the file and renames it with the date and time of closing.
It then opens a new file and writes the line there.
answers.missing: The text announces five steps but gives four; it does not say what happens to the files put aside, in particular what removes or limits them so that only seven remain.

answers.question: What does a reader see when it works, on the example the text gives?
answers.answer: The text gives no worked example; it says only that put-aside files are named log.<date-time> and that the logs never take more than about 800 megabytes, seven files put aside and the current one.
quotes: if over:      close the file; rename it to log.<date-time>
So the logs never take more than about 800 megabytes: seven files put aside and the current one.
answers.missing: A worked instance run through the steps: a file reaching a limit, its new name, the new file, and what happens to the oldest put-aside file when an eighth would be added.

unexplained.quote: So the logs never take more than about 800 megabytes: seven files put aside and the current one.

retelling.step: When a line arrives to be written, the service checks whether the current file is over 100 megabytes or older than one day.
quotes: Before each line the service checks the current file against two limits, 100 megabytes and one day.
on a line:    over = size > 100 MB or age > 1 day

retelling.step: If the file is under both limits, the line is written into the current file.
quotes: Under both limits it writes the line into the current file.
if not over:  write the line to the current file

retelling.step: If the file is over either limit, the service closes it and renames it log.<date-time> with the date and time of closing.
quotes: Over either limit it closes the file and renames it with the date and time of closing.
if over:      close the file; rename it to log.<date-time>

retelling.step: The service then opens a new file and writes the line into it.
quotes: It then opens a new file and writes the line there.
open a new file; write the line to it

gaps: The renamed files are a result no later step takes up: the text promises to say what happens to the files put aside and states that only seven are kept, but no step removes or limits them, so the announced fifth step is absent.
